findings.finding_summary: This Cochrane review of 24 double-blind trials reported that echinacea products have not been shown to provide benefits for treating colds, while noting a possible weak benefit from some products.
findings.limitations: 24 trials, 4,631 participants; authors note significant differences between the preparations tested make strong conclusions difficult

findings.endpoint: common cold prevention (risk of at least one cold)
findings.finding_summary: The same Cochrane review reported that none of the 12 prevention comparisons found a statistically significant difference, while post hoc pooling suggested a 10% to 20% relative risk reduction of questionable clinical relevance.
findings.limitations: post hoc pooling of individually non-significant trials; preparation heterogeneity

findings.finding_summary: In this randomized, blinded, controlled trial, Echinacea purpurea was reported to reduce antibiotic usage in children through prevention of respiratory tract infections.
findings.limitations: result recorded at title level this session; effect sizes pending verification

findings.finding_summary: In this randomized double-blind placebo-controlled prevention trial, Echinacea purpurea was reported to reduce the total number of cold episodes, cumulated episode days, and pain-killer medicated episodes versus placebo.
findings.limitations: attribution of the retrieved result sentence to this trial requires confirmation during verification

findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials reported that black elderberry supplementation substantially reduced upper respiratory symptoms, with a large mean effect size.
findings.limitations: 180 total participants across the included trials

findings.endpoint: cold episode duration in air travelers
findings.finding_summary: In this randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of 312 travelers, the placebo group had a significantly longer duration of cold episode days than the elderberry extract group.

findings.endpoint: common cold duration (high-dose zinc acetate lozenges)
findings.finding_summary: This systematic review reported that three trials using zinc acetate lozenges at daily doses over 75 mg showed a pooled 42% reduction in the duration of colds (95% CI 35% to 48%).
findings.limitations: three trials in the high-dose acetate pool; lozenge composition varies widely across trials

findings.finding_summary: The same review reported that five trials using total daily zinc doses below 75 mg uniformly found no effect on cold duration.
findings.limitations: five trials in the low-dose pool

findings.finding_summary: This commentary's reanalysis of the 2024 Cochrane review data reported that zinc lozenges shortened colds in adults by 37% (95% CI 27% to 46%), while noting a child trial was inconsistent with the adult trials.
findings.limitations: commentary reanalysis, not an independent review; the underlying Cochrane review's own certainty ratings were not retrieved this session

findings.population: adults with cold symptoms of less than 24 hours
findings.frequency: one lozenge every 2 hours while awake
findings.finding_summary: In this randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of 100 adults, zinc gluconate lozenges shortened cold duration by a reported 4.0 days on average (95% CI 2.3 to 5.7 days), with cough, nasal drainage, and congestion most affected.
findings.limitations: n=100, single workplace cohort (Cleveland Clinic employees); later reanalysis reported the effect concentrated in longer colds

findings.endpoint: upper respiratory tract infection severity (insoluble yeast beta-glucan)
findings.finding_summary: In this randomized double-blind placebo-controlled marathon trial, total URTI severity and symptomatic days were reported as lower with insoluble baker's yeast beta-glucan than placebo.
findings.limitations: athletic-stress population; effect differed by beta-glucan form within the same trial

findings.endpoint: upper respiratory tract infection severity (soluble yeast beta-glucan)
findings.finding_summary: In the same trial, total URTI severity with the soluble beta-glucan form was not different from placebo, though nasal discharge severity was reported as lower with both forms.
findings.limitations: athletic-stress population; form-dependent result within one trial

findings.endpoint: cold and flu symptomatic days after intense exercise
findings.finding_summary: This randomized controlled trial reported fewer cold and flu symptomatic days after intense exercise with a beverage containing dispersible yeast beta-glucan, while average URTI episode duration and count were reported as not significantly different.
findings.limitations: symptomatic-days benefit alongside null episode-count and duration results in the retrieved summary; confirm during verification

findings.endpoint: overall survival after curative gastric cancer resection (PSK adjuvant)
findings.population: patients with curatively resected gastric cancer
findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis of eight randomized controlled trials reported improved overall survival with adjuvant polysaccharide K immunochemotherapy after curative gastric cancer resection (hazard ratio 0.88, 95% CI 0.79 to 0.98).
findings.limitations: 8,009 patients; PSK is a pharmaceutical-grade protein-bound extract of turkey tail used alongside chemotherapy — results do not describe consumer mushroom supplements

findings.endpoint: 1-5 year overall survival in gastrointestinal cancer (PSK adjuvant)
findings.finding_summary: This systematic review and network meta-analysis of 23 trials reported significantly increased 1-5 year overall survival and 1-7 year disease-free survival with polysaccharide K treatment, with no increase in side effects observed.
findings.limitations: 10,684 patients; PSK is a pharmaceutical-grade protein-bound extract used adjuvant to chemotherapy — results do not describe consumer mushroom supplements
